subject: Q3 renewal: EmberTech usage & performance readout
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@embertech.com>, EmberTech Finance <finance@embertech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 renewal: EmberTech usage & performance readout

Hi Samira / Finance team,

Thanks again for the time last week — attaching the Q2 token usage export and our latency benchmark summary for the features you referenced. High-level takeaways: 

- Token spend: overall tokens are up 36% QoQ led by an embedding-heavy spike in July tied to the new search experiment. Details in embertech_q2-token-report.pdf.
- Latency: mean generation latency is stable (~180ms), but embedding calls (128-d vectors) are showing increased p95 to ~1.1s during peak windows — see latency_benchmarks.csv.
- Cost drivers: mix shift to embeddings + higher sequence lengths on summarization. We include suggested batching + quantization options that reduce per-embedding cost by ~22% in the appendix.

Given these signals, recommended renewal motion: move from month-to-month to a 12-month committed plan with a modest uplift in committed tokens and a small latency SLO addendum (we can offer a 12% term discount in exchange for a 12-month commit).

If useful, I can propose concrete committed tiers and an ops-runbook for burst handling / prefetching. Proposed next step: 30-minute sync Wed or Thu to review numbers and a draft term sheet.

Attachments: embertech_q2-token-report.pdf (token-by-service CSV), latency_benchmarks.csv (bench results)

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Samira Khan <samira@embertech.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: EmberTech Finance <finance@embertech.com>, Raj Patel <raj@embertech.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 renewal: EmberTech usage & performance readout

Michael — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few clarifying Qs before we loop in procurement: 

1) Can you break down the token spend by feature (search embeddings vs. conversation vs. summarization) for Jul/Aug/Sep? The top-line % is helpful but procurement wants the driver-level view.
2) On the embedding latency p95: is that produced by our current live model variant or from the benchmarked quantized variant referenced in the appendix? We need the live SLOs for the last 30 days.
3) If we move to the 12-month committed plan at the uplift you suggest, what is the incremental discount at 18-months vs 12? Finance asked whether a longer term unlocks a larger concession.

I'll get calendar availability for Wed/Thu after confirming with Raj and Finance.

Also tagging Raj for a quick cost-sensitivity comment — Raj, priority for us is predictable monthly billing and a way to avoid surprise overages during our holiday campaign in November.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform, EmberTech
samira@embertech.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@embertech.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 renewal: EmberTech usage & performance readout

Hey Samira — quick operational notes from the CS / infra side that should answer Q2 and help the renewal conversation: 

- Latency origin: the p95 increase is observed on production (the live model) specifically during your peak batch windows (15:00–17:00 PT). The attached CSV shows live-run sampling timestamps flagged where p95 exceeded 900ms.
- Root cause: two concurrent factors — (a) embedding requests spiking with smaller batch sizes from your collector job and (b) occasional preemption delays on the dedicated nodes we use for your account during cross-region fallbacks. We have three mitigations: larger client-side batching, pre-warming a modest dedicated pool at peak hours, or routing embedding traffic to an alternate region with lower contention.
- Cost impact: switching to the recommended 4x batching pattern reduces per-embedding cost ~20% with negligible impact to median latency. The quantized runtime is slightly faster for CPU-heavy fallbacks but the live variant numbers above are from the unquantized production model.

I can put together an ops runbook with traffic shaping examples and a one-week pilot for pre-warming if the team wants to see concrete numbers.

Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@embertech.com>, EmberTech Finance <finance@embertech.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: term & capacity options (summary)

Samira / Finance — following up with concrete options so you have something to circulate internally. I kept the tiers tight to reflect the July/Aug spikes and the November campaign risk Samira noted.

Option A (12-mo, moderate uplift)
- Commit: +40% committed tokens vs current run-rate
- Price: 12% upfront term discount, fixed unit price for committed tokens, overages billed at standard rate
- Ops: included 4 pre-warmed GPU-hours/day during 15:00–17:00 PT weekdays (costs rolled into the commitment)

Option B (18-mo, lock + deeper discount)
- Commit: +35% committed tokens (lower uplift)
- Price: 16% term discount (longer lock in exchange for reduced uplift)
- Ops: same pre-warm footprint, plus a one-week pilot to validate batching changes

Notes: both options include a quarterly review and can be amended after the November campaign if you provide us a forecast 30 days in advance. Attached is a short term sheet I can convert to DocuSign.

Next steps: if Finance prefers Option B we can price it out and send a draft on DocuSign (link below). If you'd like, Michael and Laura can run a 30-minute pilot kickoff to validate the pre-warm + batching play.

DocuSign draft (preview): https://www.docusign.com/Seq/ABC-123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-2026-ET-042

Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

From: Samira Khan <samira@embertech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: EmberTech Finance <finance@embertech.com>, Raj Patel <raj@embertech.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: term & capacity options (summary)

Appreciate the clear options. Finance is leaning toward Option B (we value predictability and would consider the slightly longer lock if the economics are better). Two asks before we proceed: 

1) Please send the month-by-month feature-level spend for Jul/Aug/Sep (as Samira requested) so we can validate the uplift assumptions.
2) Add a one-line carve-out in the DocuSign draft for the November campaign window to allow a one-time short-term burst credit if we exceed agreed thresholds due to holiday traffic.

We will review the proposal with procurement this afternoon and aim to respond with a redline or acceptance by Friday EOD. Please hold Wed 23 Sep 10:00–10:30 PT for a follow-up if we need to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Samira
